by: session, Adrian 16 Oct 2026: 'put each common mistake at the end of its clip as a Watch out step'

beats.say: Solve seven to the power X minus one equals five to the power X minus three.
asks: Can I make the bases the same?

beats.say: Seven and five cannot be made the same base. The plan: take log on both sides, then bring the powers down.
asks: Why take lg of both sides?
Can I use ln instead of lg?

beats.say: Bring down the powers. Each power comes down in front of its log.

do.text: Bring down power: $\lg x^r = r\lg x$

asks: Why can the power come down?

beats.say: So X minus one, times log seven, equals X minus three, times log five.
Log seven and log five are just numbers. Expand the brackets as usual.
asks: Why is lg 7 just a number?

beats.say: Put the X terms on the left, and the number terms on the right.
asks: Why move the x terms to the left?

beats.say: Factorise out X, then divide by log seven minus log five.
Press calculator. X is about minus eight point five seven.
asks: How do I key this in?

beats.say: Watch out: the calculator shows minus eight point five six six five four. Rounding never removes a minus.
